messages:
kai: noticing p95 jump on production serving cluster in eu-west-1 around 14:05 UTC, from ~120ms to ~780ms. correlating with one tenant's batch sizes spiking.

maria: @kai seen the dashboards, throughput drops on node-pool-b, CPU stays okay, GPU utilization spikes then drops. looks like kernel fallback thrashing.

ajay: can we surface which kernel pairs switched? I think our kernel selector fell back to slower fp16->int8 path because of sequence length outliers.

kai: pulling profiler traces now. quick grep shows frequent fallback: "selected_kernel: aten_gemm_fp16 -> fallback_quantized" repeated 1.2k times in 5m.

linh: inc-bot posted an alert: "latency_surge eu-west-1 serving-runtime p95>500ms" and routed to #eng-oncall.

sre-bot: automatic mitigation rule triggered: reduced max_batch_size from 32 -> 16 for pool node-pool-b (policy: latency-first).

maria: that likely mitigated some tails, but we're still seeing KV cache eviction churn. tenant X is showing high prefix variance causing KV growth and eviction thrash.

ajay: hypothesis: large variance in prompt lengths causes kernel selection path to flip and KV cache to be reallocated. we should pin kernel hints for the problematic model version while we investigate.

kai: I can flip a feature flag to force kernel_hint=fast-attn for model:redwood-open-7b:v2 on affected pool. would that be safe?

linh: do it for canary subset (10% routing). add extra logging for selected kernel and kvcache_hits.

ajay: command we used: 
```
redwoodctl feature-flag set kernel_hint.force=fast-attn --model redwood-open-7b:v2 --pool node-pool-b --percent 10
```
(rolled at 14:22 UTC)

maria: after canary flip, p95 dropped to ~210ms on canary routing, overall cluster p95 improved to ~330ms. good sign.

kai: enabling extra batching heuristics: ttl for prefix grouping lowered from 200ms -> 80ms to reduce cross-request batch variability.

linh: increased KV cache size on pool by +8% to reduce eviction frequency as a temporary lift. will monitor memory.

ajay: we should also add a guard in kernel selector: if fallback rate > 5% in 1m, throttle incoming large batches and route to warm pool with quantized kernels.

maria: created ticket PERF-789: add fallback-rate circuit and routing fallback policy + unit tests. linking traces and flame graphs in ticket.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (feature flag canary, batch-ttl reduced, cache size increased). severity lowered to S2. next update in 30m.

kai: follow-up actions: (1) daily preflight profiling to detect sequence-length skews, (2) permanent kernel hint to model:v2 after QA, (3) tuning of batch heuristics in runtime.

linh: quick note: we saw one noisy neighbor that launched a heavy calibration job on same node-pool around 14:03 — talking to infra to put calibration jobs on isolated maintenance pool.

ajay: logs we added (sample): 
```
[14:21:45] model=redwood-open-7b:v2 sel=fast-attn kv_hits=0.64 batch=28 -> kernel=fast-attn
[14:21:46] model=redwood-open-7b:v2 sel=fast-attn kv_hits=0.12 batch=31 -> kernel=fallback-quant
```
shows low kv_hits correlate with fallback.

maria: thanks team. I'll draft a short customer-facing blurb for accounts potentially impacted. keeping this thread for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

kai: +1, will attach flame graphs to PERF-789 and schedule follow-up eng-runtime/eng-infra sync.

linh: monitoring until 15:00 UTC, will report any regressions.

inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: final update at 15:22 UTC — traffic normalized, long-term work queued under PERF-789 and INFRA-101.
